beats.visual: golden palace by the river Sarayu
beats.text: On the banks of the Sarayu stood Ayodhya, a city of peace and dharma.
Its king, Dasharatha, had wealth, power and his people's love. But he had no son.
On Sage Vasishtha's advice, he performed the Putrakameshti Yagna.

beats.visual: a divine being rising from the flames with a bowl of kheer
beats.text: From the fire rose a divine being. 'Share this kheer among your queens,' he said.
And so began the story that would shape the world.
Queen Kaushalya gave birth to Rama, the embodiment of dharma.
Kaikeyi gave birth to Bharata. Sumitra gave birth to twins, Lakshmana and Shatrughna.
The four grew up inseparable. Lakshmana's heart belonged to Rama, and Shatrughna's to Bharata.
They mastered scriptures, archery and the duties of a righteous king.
Even as a boy, Rama was kind to everyone.
Demons were destroying the prayers of the sages. Vishwamitra came to Ayodhya for help.
'Send Rama and Lakshmana with me.' Dasharatha was heartbroken, but Rama went willingly.
On the road, Vishwamitra taught them divine weapons and mantras.
Then came Tataka, a fearsome demoness who terrorized the forest.
Rama's arrow struck true. The forest was free again.

beats.visual: sages at a yagna, fire glowing
beats.text: At Siddhashrama, Vishwamitra began a sacred yagna. Rama and Lakshmana guarded it for six days and nights.
On the last day, the demon Subahu and his general Maricha attacked.
Rama's Manava astra hurled Maricha far across the ocean. Subahu fell to the Agni astra.
The yagna was complete. The sages were free.
On the road to Mithila, they found an empty ashram, silent for centuries.
Ahalya, wife of Sage Gautama, had been cursed to live unseen until Rama came.
As Rama entered, the curse broke. Ahalya appeared, radiant and free.
She bowed in gratitude. Her long penance had ended." On- screen: Rama's grace frees all.
King Janaka of Mithila welcomed the princes with honor.

beats.visual: a giant bow on an iron cart pulled by many men
beats.text: In his palace lay Shiva's mighty bow. Not even gods and demons could lift it.
Janaka had made a vow: whoever strings this bow will marry his daughter, Sita.
Vishwamitra knew exactly why he had brought Rama here.
Years earlier, King Janaka was ploughing a field for a sacred ritual.

beats.visual: a golden casket rising from the furrow
beats.text: From the earth emerged a glowing child.
He named her Sita, meaning 'furrow.' Born of the Earth, she was raised as his own.

beats.visual: young Sita lifting the heavy bow with ease
beats.text: As a girl, she once moved Shiva's bow like a toy. Janaka knew she was no ordinary child.
Kings from across the land came to win Sita's hand. One by one, they failed.
Even mighty Ravana was crushed under the bow and left in shame.
Then Rama stepped forward. He bowed to his teacher and lifted the bow.
As he drew the string, it broke in two with a crack that shook Mithila.
Sita placed the garland around Rama's neck." On- screen: Two souls, one destiny.

beats.visual: Janaka sending a message to Ayodhya
beats.text: Janaka sent word to Dasharatha, who arrived with his entire court.

beats.visual: Janaka with his four daughters and niece
beats.text: Janaka offered his daughters to all four princes: Sita to Rama, Urmila to Lakshmana, Mandavi to Bharata, Shrutakirti to Shatrughna.
Four brothers married four sisters in one grand ceremony.
The whole city sang and danced for days.

beats.visual: the wedding procession on the road home
beats.text: On the way back to Ayodhya, a storm rose and a fearsome sage blocked the path.

beats.visual: Parashurama with his axe, eyes blazing
beats.text: It was Parashurama, who had wiped out proud kings twenty-one times. 'You broke Shiva's bow. Now string Vishnu's.'
Rama took the bow, strung it and fixed an arrow in one smooth motion.
Parashurama recognized the truth and withdrew in peace.

title: The Coronation Plan

beats.text: For twelve years, Ayodhya was happy under Dasharatha. But the king was growing old.
He decided it was time to crown Rama as the next king. The whole court agreed.
News spread, and the city burst into celebration.
Only Rama stayed quiet and humble. He never wanted the throne.

onscreen: Tomorrow, a king would be crowned…

beats.visual: Manthara watching the celebration with a sour face
beats.text: Kaikeyi's maid Manthara could not bear the joy. She ran to her queen.
'Rama becomes king tomorrow, and your son Bharata will be nothing. Remember the two boons the king once gave you?'
At first Kaikeyi loved Rama as her own son. But slowly, the poison of doubt took hold.

beats.visual: Kaikeyi removing her jewels, lying on the floor
beats.text: She went to the anger chamber and waited for the king.
Dasharatha found his beloved queen on the floor. 'Ask anything,' he said.
'Two boons you promised me long ago. First: Bharata becomes king. Second: Rama goes to the forest for fourteen years.'
The king fell to the ground. He begged, wept and pleaded. Kaikeyi did not move.

beats.visual: night passing, the king awake in grief
beats.text: A king bound by his word. A father bound by love.

title: Rama Accepts Exile

beats.visual: Rama arriving at the palace at dawn
beats.text: Rama came to greet his father and found him broken.
Kaikeyi told him everything. Rama did not argue or frown.
'If my father's word needs it, I go gladly. Why would I need the crown when I have his honor?'

beats.visual: Rama removing his royal robes, putting on bark cloth
beats.text: He gave up a kingdom as easily as one lets go of a flower.

onscreen: The kingdom lost. The dharma kept.

beats.text: Rama asked Sita to stay behind. 'The forest is hard and dangerous.'
'Where you are is my home. Even a palace without you is a jungle,' she said.
Lakshmana too refused to be left behind. 'I will serve you day and night.'

beats.visual: three figures leaving the palace gate
beats.text: The three left Ayodhya in bark cloth, and the whole city followed them in tears.

beats.visual: a wide river at dawn, a boatman waiting
beats.text: At the Ganga, the boatman king Guha welcomed Rama as a dear friend.
He begged them to stay in his kingdom, but Rama refused. He had a vow to keep.
Guha rowed them across. Sita prayed to the Ganga for their safe return.

beats.visual: Rama cutting his hair into a sage's matted locks
beats.text: Here Rama gave up the last sign of royalty and became a forest sage.

title: Dasharatha's Death

beats.text: With Rama gone, Ayodhya lost its light.
Dasharatha cried Rama's name day and night. He remembered a curse from long ago, when he had accidentally killed a young hermit's son.

beats.visual: the old blind parents of the hermit
beats.text: The grieving parents had cursed him to die of the same sorrow.

beats.visual: the king whispering 'Rama...' in his last breath
beats.text: On the sixth night, he whispered 'Rama, Rama,' and was gone.

onscreen: A father who died of love.

beats.visual: Bharata riding home from his uncle's kingdom
beats.text: Bharata was away when all this happened. Messengers called him home in haste.
He felt something was wrong the moment he saw the silent city.
Kaikeyi proudly told him: 'Your father is gone. Rama is in exile. The throne is yours.'
Bharata was shattered. 'You have destroyed my family for my sake? I want nothing of this.'
He refused the crown and set out to bring his brother home.

beats.visual: Bharata and the whole city marching into the forest
beats.text: Bharata led an army of citizens, queens and sages to find Rama.
At Chitrakoot, he fell at Rama's feet, weeping. 'Return and rule, brother.'
Rama embraced him. 'Our father gave his word. I must keep it, and you must rule.'
Bharata would not give in. For hours, two brothers each tried to give the kingdom to the other.
At last, Bharata asked for one thing: 'Give me your sandals.'

beats.visual: Rama placing his sandals in Bharata's hands
beats.text: Rama agreed. Bharata carried them on his head all the way home.

beats.visual: the sandals on the throne of Ayodhya
beats.text: He placed them on the throne and ruled in Rama's name, as a servant.

beats.visual: Bharata living in a simple hut outside the city
beats.text: He lived like an ascetic for fourteen years, waiting for his brother.

title: Atri and Anasuya

beats.text: Deep in the forest, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana visited Sage Atri's ashram.
Atri's wife, Anasuya, a woman of great virtue, embraced Sita like a daughter.

beats.visual: Anasuya giving Sita jewels and a garland
beats.text: She gave her divine gifts: a garland that never withers and clothes that never fade.
She spoke to Sita about devotion and strength, wisdom Sita would need in the days ahead.

onscreen: A blessing for what was to come.

title: Viradha

beats.text: As they moved deeper into Dandaka forest, a terrible demon, Viradha, rose before them.
He snatched Sita and mocked the princes.
Rama and Lakshmana's arrows struck again and again, but the demon could not be killed by weapons.

beats.visual: the princes burying him in a pit
beats.text: At last, they buried him alive. Before dying, he revealed he was a cursed celestial, now free.

onscreen: The first demon. Not the last.

beats.text: Sage Agastya guided them to Panchavati, a lovely land beside the Godavari.
Lakshmana built a simple cottage of leaves and bamboo.

beats.visual: the three sitting by the river at sunset
beats.text: For a while, they lived in peace. Deer came close. Birds sang at dawn.
These were the happiest days of their exile. But a storm was already on its way.

title: Surpanakha

beats.visual: a demoness watching Rama from the trees
beats.text: One day, Ravana's sister Surpanakha saw Rama and fell in love.

beats.visual: her turning into a beautiful woman
beats.text: She took a beautiful form and asked him to marry her.
Rama said, 'I am married. Ask my brother.' Lakshmana laughed and refused too.
Furious, she lunged at Sita. Lakshmana struck first and cut off her nose and ears.
Bleeding and burning with hatred, she fled to her brothers.

onscreen: An insult that would burn Lanka.

beats.text: Surpanakha begged her brother Khara for revenge.
Khara sent fourteen warriors. Rama killed all of them.

beats.visual: a vast demon army, thousands strong
beats.text: Khara and Dushana then brought fourteen thousand demons to the forest.
Rama sent Sita and Lakshmana to a cave and faced the army alone. His arrows filled the sky.
By evening, the entire army lay still.

beats.visual: Surpanakha before Ravana in his court
beats.text: Surpanakha flew to Lanka and showed her wounds to Ravana.
She described Sita's beauty and goaded him: 'Take her, and destroy Rama.'
Ravana went to Maricha, the demon Rama had once thrown across the ocean.
'Do not touch Rama,' Maricha begged. 'I have felt his arrow.' But Ravana threatened him, and Maricha agreed.

beats.visual: a shimmering golden deer near the hut
beats.text: One morning, Sita saw a deer with a golden coat and silver spots.
'Rama, please catch it for me!'
Lakshmana was uneasy. 'Brother, it could be a demon's trick.'
But Rama could not refuse Sita. 'Guard her well,' he said, and followed the deer into the forest.

beats.visual: the deer leading him far away
beats.text: The deer led him deeper and deeper, away from the hut.

title: The Lakshman Rekha

beats.text: Far away, Rama's arrow hit the deer, and it turned back into Maricha.
With his dying breath, he cried out in Rama's voice: 'Sita! Lakshmana!'
Sita heard it and begged Lakshmana to go. He hesitated. She spoke harsh words in fear.

beats.visual: Lakshmana drawing a line around the hut
beats.text: Hurt but obedient, he drew a line around the hut. 'Do not cross this, whatever happens.'
Then he went to find his brother.

onscreen: The line that must not be crossed.

beats.visual: a sage at the door, begging
beats.text: As soon as he left, a sage came to the hut asking for alms.
Sita saw nothing wrong with the old man. She offered food from inside the line.

beats.visual: the sage refusing, demanding she step out
beats.text: He insisted she come out. She stepped over the line.

beats.visual: the sage revealing ten heads, Ravana
beats.text: The sage turned into Ravana, king of Lanka.
He seized her and flew into the sky. Sita's cries echoed across the forest.

title: Jatayu

beats.visual: the great vulture on a tree
beats.text: Jatayu, an old vulture and friend of Dasharatha, heard Sita's cries.
Though weak with age, he attacked Ravana with all his strength.
He broke the chariot and wounded the demon king.
But Ravana drew his sword and cut off the old bird's wings. Jatayu fell.
He lived long enough to tell Rama everything. Rama performed his funeral like a son.

onscreen: A bird who gave his life for dharma.

beats.visual: Rama and Lakshmana searching the forest
beats.text: Rama and Lakshmana searched everywhere for Sita, calling her name.

beats.visual: a huge headless demon with long arms
beats.text: Suddenly, a giant demon named Kabandha seized them in his arms.

beats.visual: the brothers cutting off his arms
beats.text: They sliced off his arms, and Kabandha cried out in relief.

beats.visual: a radiant being rising from the fire
beats.text: He had been a cursed celestial. Freed by Rama, he gave them a clue: 'Seek Sugriva, king of the monkeys, at Mount Rishyamukha.'" On- screen: A clue in the darkness.

beats.visual: an old woman sweeping a forest path
beats.text: Near Lake Pampa lived Shabari, an aged devotee who had waited years for Rama.

beats.visual: Shabari carrying a basket of berries
beats.text: Each day she gathered the sweetest berries, tasting each one to be sure it was good.

beats.visual: Rama eating the berries with joy
beats.text: When Rama finally came, he happily ate the berries she had already tasted.
He cared nothing for rank or custom. He saw only her love.

beats.visual: Sugriva watching from a mountain, afraid
beats.text: On Rishyamukha, the exiled monkey king Sugriva saw two warriors approaching and sent his minister, Hanuman, to check.

beats.visual: Hanuman disguised as a humble brahmin
beats.text: Hanuman came disguised as a priest and spoke so wisely that Rama turned to Lakshmana in wonder.

beats.visual: Hanuman revealing his true form, bowing
beats.text: Hanuman fell at Rama's feet, knowing instantly who he was.

beats.visual: Hanuman lifting both brothers on his shoulders
beats.text: He carried them to Sugriva. A lifelong devotion had begun.

beats.visual: Rama and Sugriva before a sacred fire
beats.text: Rama and Sugriva sealed their friendship before a sacred fire.
Sugriva's brother Vali had stolen his kingdom and his wife. 'Help me,' he said, 'and my army will find Sita.'
Rama promised to defeat Vali.

beats.visual: Sugriva showing Sita's jewels, dropped as she was carried away
beats.text: Sugriva showed him jewels Sita had dropped from the sky. Rama held them and wept.

beats.visual: Sugriva challenging Vali at his gate
beats.text: Sugriva challenged Vali to a duel. Vali, the mightiest monkey, was said to take half the strength of any enemy.
The two looked alike, and Rama hesitated to shoot, fearing he might hit the wrong one.

beats.visual: Sugriva wearing a garland as a mark
beats.text: The next day Sugriva wore a garland. This time Rama's arrow flew true.
Vali asked, 'Why strike from hiding?' Rama explained his duty. Vali accepted and blessed his son, Angada.
With the monsoon season, no army could march. Rama and Lakshmana waited on a mountain.

beats.visual: Rama gazing at the sky, alone
beats.text: Every night, Rama grieved for Sita. The storms only made it harder.

beats.visual: Sugriva enjoying luxury in his palace
beats.text: Meanwhile, Sugriva fell into comfort and forgot his promise.

beats.visual: Lakshmana storming into the city, bow in hand
beats.text: When the rains ended, an angry Lakshmana came to remind him. Sugriva was ashamed and ordered his armies to gather.

beats.visual: monkey armies leaving in four directions
beats.text: Sugriva sent search parties to the east, west, north and south.
Rama gave Hanuman his signet ring. 'Show this to Sita. She will know you come from me.'

beats.visual: the southern party led by Angada, Jambavan and Hanuman
beats.text: The southern party, led by Prince Angada, searched cave after cave.

beats.visual: monkeys sitting hopelessly on a beach
beats.text: A month passed. They found nothing, and the deadline was gone. Despair settled in.

beats.visual: the great vulture Sampati, wingless on a cliff
beats.text: On the shore, they met Sampati, brother of the fallen Jatayu.
With his sharp vulture eyes he saw far across the ocean. 'I see Lanka, and a woman weeping in a garden,' he said.

beats.visual: the monkeys staring at the endless sea
beats.text: Lanka was a hundred yojanas away across the water. None of them could cross.
Jambavan, the wise old bear, knew who could. He turned to Hanuman." On- screen: Who can cross the ocean?

beats.visual: Hanuman sitting alone, forgetting his powers
beats.text: As a child, a curse had made Hanuman forget his own strength.
Jambavan spoke of his birth, his speed and his courage. Slowly, Hanuman remembered.

beats.visual: Hanuman growing to a mountain's size
beats.text: He grew vast as a mountain and stood on Mount Mahendra. The earth trembled.
'Jai Shri Ram!' he roared, and leapt toward Lanka.
Gods tested Hanuman on his flight. First, the sea-serpent Surasa rose with a huge open mouth.

beats.visual: Hanuman shrinking and slipping out of her mouth
beats.text: Hanuman grew larger, then shrank to a thumb's size and slipped through her jaws. She blessed him.

beats.visual: the shadow-demoness Simhika reaching up from the water
beats.text: Next, Simhika grabbed his shadow and dragged him down.
Hanuman entered her body and tore free. The sea was clear.

beats.visual: golden Lanka glowing on the horizon
beats.text: At last Hanuman landed on Lanka, a city of gold with towering walls.

beats.visual: Hanuman shrinking to the size of a cat
beats.text: He shrank to the size of a cat and crept toward the gate in the night.

beats.visual: Lankini, the guardian demoness, blocking him
beats.text: Lankini, the city's guardian, stopped him. 'No one enters Lanka.'

beats.visual: Hanuman striking her once with his left hand
beats.text: Hanuman struck her lightly. She fell, remembering Brahma's old prophecy: when a monkey defeats her, Lanka's end is near.

beats.visual: Hanuman searching Ravana's palace at night
beats.text: Hanuman searched Ravana's palace room by room, but found no Sita.

beats.visual: Hanuman gazing at a garden of Ashoka trees
beats.text: At last he saw a garden of Ashoka trees, and beneath one, a thin, pale woman in plain clothes.
Ferocious demonesses guarded her. She wept, whispering Rama's name.

beats.visual: Hanuman hiding in the tree above
beats.text: Hanuman hid in the branches above, his heart pounding. He had found her.

beats.visual: Ravana threatening Sita in the garden
beats.text: At dawn, Ravana came to the garden. 'Marry me, or I will kill you in two months.'
Sita placed a blade of grass between them and refused to even look at him.
Ravana stormed away. The demonesses taunted her until she was alone.

beats.visual: Hanuman softly singing Rama's story from the tree
beats.text: Then a gentle voice from the tree began to sing the story of Rama.

title: The Ring and the Jewel

beats.visual: Hanuman dropping Rama's ring into Sita's hands
beats.text: Hanuman dropped Rama's ring into her lap. Sita wept with joy.
She wondered if this was another demon's trick, but Hanuman's kind words won her trust.

beats.visual: Hanuman offering to carry her away
beats.text: He offered to carry her back right then. 'No,' said Sita. 'Rama must come and rescue me himself, for his honor.'

beats.visual: Sita giving her jewel, the Choodamani
beats.text: She gave him her hair jewel as proof. 'Tell Rama I am waiting.'

onscreen: A message. A jewel. A hope.

beats.text: Before leaving, Hanuman wanted to test Ravana's strength. He tore through the palace garden.

beats.visual: Hanuman fighting the guards and Akshayakumara
beats.text: Guards came and fell. Ravana's own son Akshayakumara fell too.
Hanuman allowed Indrajit to bind him, so he could meet Ravana. He warned him: 'Return Sita, or face Rama.'

beats.visual: a burning tail, Hanuman leaping over rooftops
beats.text: Ravana ordered his tail set on fire. Hanuman broke free and burned Lanka to the ground, sparing only where Sita sat." On- screen: Lanka in flames.

beats.visual: Hanuman flying back over the ocean
beats.text: Hanuman flew back to Mahendra mountain, where the monkeys cheered his return.
He told Rama everything: 'I have seen Sita. She is alive and faithful.'
He placed her jewel in Rama's hands. Rama held it to his heart and wept.
'I have nothing to give you, Hanuman, but this embrace.'

beats.visual: millions of monkeys and bears marching
beats.text: Sugriva's army set out for the southern shore, millions strong.
They reached the sea and stopped. How could an army cross such water?

beats.visual: Rama sitting in prayer on the shore
beats.text: Rama sat on the shore and prayed to Samudra, the ocean god, for three days.
The sea did not answer.
In Lanka, Ravana's younger brother Vibhishana begged him: 'Return Sita and end this war.'

beats.visual: Ravana kicking him from the throne
beats.text: Ravana kicked him out of the court in a rage.

beats.visual: Vibhishana crossing the sky to Rama's camp
beats.text: Vibhishana flew to Rama's camp and asked for refuge. Many advisors warned it was a trick.
But Rama said, 'I never turn away someone who seeks shelter.' He crowned him king of Lanka that day." On- screen: Refuge for all who ask.

beats.visual: Rama raising his bow at the ocean
beats.text: When Samudra still did not appear, Rama raised his bow to dry up the sea.
The ocean god rose in fear and begged for mercy. 'Build a bridge,' he advised. 'I will hold it.'

beats.visual: Nala and Neel directing the work
beats.text: The engineers Nala and Neel guided the work.
Monkeys carried boulders, each marked with Rama's name. The stones floated. In five days, the bridge to Lanka was ready.
Before war, Rama gave Ravana one last chance. He sent Prince Angada as his messenger.
Angada walked into the demon king's court without fear.
'Return Sita,' he said. When the court laughed, he planted his foot and said, 'If any of you can move it, Rama will go home.'

beats.visual: warriors failing to lift his foot
beats.text: No one could. Ravana did not listen. The last chance for peace was gone.

beats.visual: two vast armies facing each other across Lanka's plain
beats.text: Rama's monkey army stood before Ravana's demon legions.

beats.visual: Rama and Lakshmana at the front
beats.text: Rama and Lakshmana led from the front. On the walls, Ravana watched with his ten heads.

beats.visual: boulders and trees hurled at the gates
beats.text: The monkeys charged with rocks, trees and bare hands.

beats.visual: Hanuman and Angada fighting demon generals
beats.text: Demon generals fell one by one to Hanuman, Angada and Sugriva. But Ravana's son Indrajit was yet to fight.

beats.visual: Indrajit hiding in the clouds, invisible
beats.text: Indrajit, master of illusion, fought from the clouds where no one could see him.

beats.visual: serpent arrows binding Rama and Lakshmana
beats.text: He shot the Nagapasha, arrows of living serpents, which bound both brothers.
The brothers fell, and the monkey army thought they were gone.
Then Garuda, the eagle king and enemy of serpents, swept in. The snakes fled, and the brothers rose.
The fighting grew fiercer each day. Indrajit struck again and again.
At last he threw the deadly Shakti spear at Lakshmana.
Lakshmana fell, unconscious and barely breathing.
Rama held him and wept. 'I can find another wife. I cannot find another brother.'
The physician Sushena said: 'There is one hope: the Sanjeevani herb, before sunrise.'

title: Sanjeevani

beats.text: Sanjeevani grew on a faraway mountain in the Himalayas. Hanuman flew there in a single night.

beats.visual: many glowing herbs on the peak
beats.text: But the mountain glowed with countless herbs, and he could not tell which was the right one.
So Hanuman lifted the whole mountain and carried it across the sky.

beats.visual: Lakshmana awakening as Sushena applies the herb
beats.text: Sushena found the herb. Lakshmana opened his eyes just before dawn.

onscreen: A brother brought back from the edge.

beats.visual: Ravana ordering his sleeping giant brother woken
beats.text: Ravana's brother Kumbhakarna slept for six months at a time. The demons woke him with drums and elephants.
He told Ravana the truth: 'Sita's capture was wrong.' But he still chose to fight for his brother.

beats.visual: the giant crushing the monkey army
beats.text: He was as tall as a mountain, and monkeys scattered in fear.
Rama's arrows finally brought him down. He died with honor.

beats.visual: Indrajit performing a secret fire ritual
beats.text: Indrajit slipped away to perform a sacred ritual that would make him unbeatable.

beats.visual: Vibhishana pointing out the hidden place
beats.text: Vibhishana knew the secret and led Lakshmana to the ritual grounds.

beats.visual: Lakshmana attacking before the ritual ended
beats.text: Lakshmana broke the ritual and challenged Indrajit.

beats.visual: a fierce duel in the sky
beats.text: After a terrible fight, Lakshmana's arrow found its mark. Ravana's greatest warrior was no more.

beats.visual: Ravana in his golden chariot, eyes burning
beats.text: Mad with grief, Ravana rode out himself.

beats.visual: Rama on foot against the demon king's chariot
beats.text: Rama had no chariot, so Indra sent his own divine chariot with its charioteer Matali.
For days they fought, arrow against arrow. Every time Rama cut off a head, another grew.
Rama could not defeat Ravana by ordinary means.
Vibhishana whispered the secret: 'Ravana's life is hidden in the nectar in his navel.'

beats.visual: Matali reminding Rama of the Brahmastra
beats.text: Matali reminded Rama of the Brahmastra, the weapon of Brahma.
Rama chanted a mantra and released it.
The arrow struck Ravana's navel. The mighty king of Lanka fell.
Even then, Rama asked Vibhishana to give his brother a proper funeral.

beats.visual: Sita walking out of the Ashok Vatika
beats.text: After the war, Hanuman brought word of victory to Sita. She was free at last.

beats.visual: Rama seeing Sita, silent and still
beats.text: When they met, Rama asked her to prove her purity before the world, for the sake of the people's trust.

beats.visual: Sita asking Lakshmana to build a pyre
beats.text: Sita, hurt but unbroken, stepped into the fire.

beats.visual: Agni, the fire god, lifting Sita unharmed
beats.text: Agni himself rose from the flames and returned her to Rama. 'She is pure,' he said.

beats.visual: the flying Pushpak Vimana carrying Rama, Sita, Lakshmana
beats.text: The fourteen years of exile were ending. Rama, Sita and Lakshmana flew home in the Pushpak Vimana.
Bharata waited at the gates, holding the paduka, exactly as he had for fourteen years.
The brothers embraced, and the sandals were laid at Rama's feet.
That night, the whole city lit lamps to welcome their king home. We still celebrate that night as Diwali.
Rama was crowned king, and the golden age of Ram Rajya began.
